52.0.s.en: (1) The rebellion against Babylon and the fall of Jerusalem

52.0.0.en: After Babylon took Jehoiachin, king of Judah, captive, the king of Babylon chose his uncle Mattaniah in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah (2 Kgs 24:17), and made him king when he was twenty-one years old. He was weak in character: he would show his loyalty to Babylon, then turn back and speak with Egypt, and he cast Jeremiah into prison, then turned back and consulted him. The reign of Zedekiah lasted 11 years, in which he lost his ability to lead his people and lost the trust of Babylon in him. This was by God's ordering, to discipline Zedekiah and all his kingdom because of their sins.

52.1.0.en: Zedekiah walked in evil like his brother Jehoiakim, although he sometimes pretended to submit to God and to His prophet Jeremiah.

52.2.0.en: The reign of Zedekiah over the kingdom of Judah ended with his rebellion against the king of Babylon, so the latter rose against him, took him captive, and shattered and burned Jerusalem because of the sins of her people.

52.3.0.en: In the ninth year of King Zedekiah the armies of Babylon came and besieged Jerusalem and built around her ramparts and towers, to prevent her people from escaping from her, to be able to know what was going on inside her, and to make it easy to break into her. This was in the month of January of the year 588 BC, which corresponds to the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of the reign of Zedekiah.

52.4.0.en: The siege of Jerusalem continued for a year and a half, that is, until the month of July of the year 587 BC, which corresponds to the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year of King Zedekiah. At this time the famine became severe among the inhabitants of Jerusalem until they were nearly dying, so they looked for a way to flee and save themselves.

52.5.0.en: In a last attempt to escape, the Jews made a breach in the wall of the city and went out through it. It was between the two walls, near the king's garden.

52.5.1.en: If you want to overcome your enemies the demons, you must rely on God and not on your own thoughts or strength, because they are stronger than you, and in this way you save yourself from their hands however much their tricks and wars surround you.

52.5.3.en: 8- But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.

52.5.4.en: 9- Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; where he gave judgment upon him. 10- And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: he slew also all the princes of Judah in Riblah. 11- Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in two chains of brass, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

52.6.0.en: The plains of Jericho: a valley next to the city of Jericho, which lies beside the river Jordan, northeast of Jerusalem.

52.6.1.en: King Zedekiah fled from the city of Jerusalem, but the armies of Babylon were able to seize him when he reached the plains of Jericho.

52.7.0.en: Riblah: a city near Hamath and the river Orontes, which is now in Syria, and lies north of Jericho. The soldiers of Babylon took King Zedekiah and went with him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was staying in Riblah to prevent any Egyptian reinforcements from reaching the Jews from the Egyptians living there, and because there is a trade route between Egypt and Babylon.

52.7.1.en: V. 10: In order to frighten and humiliate Zedekiah, Nebuchadnezzar killed his sons before his eyes, then the princes of his people.

52.8.0.en: Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with chains of brass, that is, strong chains so that he would not flee, and led him captive to Babylon and cast him into prison until the end of his life.

52.8.1.en: Nebuchadnezzar humiliated Zedekiah, and years later Nebuchadnezzar lost his reason and was cast out like the animals, away from people, for a period of seven years. Do not humiliate others lest you be humiliated, and do not wrong anyone, but be merciful and you will obtain the mercies of God.

52.8.2.en: [3] The fall of Jerusalem and the plundering of the temple (vv. 12-23)

52.8.3.en: 12- Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, which served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem, 13- And burned the house of the LORD, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and all the houses of the great men, burned he with fire. 14- And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down all the walls of Jerusalem round about. 15- Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive certain of the poor of the people, and the residue of the people that remained in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude. 16- But Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and for husbandmen. 17- Also the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans brake, and carried all the brass of them to Babylon. 18- The caldrons also, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the bowls, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away. 19- And the basons, and the firepans, and the bowls, and the caldrons, and the candlesticks, and the spoons, and the cups; that which was of gold in gold, and that which was of silver in silver, took the captain of the guard away. 20- The two pillars, one sea, and twelve brazen bulls that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the LORD: the brass of all these vessels was without weight. 21- And concerning the pillars, the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits; and a fillet of twelve cubits did compass it; and the thickness thereof was four fingers: it was hollow.

52.8.4.en: 22- And a chapiter of brass was upon it; and the height of one chapiter was five cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the chapiters round about, all of brass. The second pillar also and the pomegranates were like unto these. 23- And there were ninety and six pomegranates on a side; and all the pomegranates upon the network were an hundred round about.

52.9.0.en: After the capture of Jerusalem, the taking of the king captive, the killing of the great men, and the captivity of many to Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar sent the captain of the guard, who represents the commander of the army or the minister of the interior, and who was called Nebuzaradan, to Jerusalem. This was on the tenth day of the fifth month in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

52.10.0.en: The work of Nebuzaradan was the complete destruction of Jerusalem, so that she would never think of rebelling against Babylon. So he burned the temple of Solomon, the king's palace, and the palaces of the great men, after plundering what was in them. The first plundering of the temple had been completed by Babylon in the year 597 BC, when she took the silver and gold that were in it.

52.11.0.en: Nebuzaradan also tore down the walls of Jerusalem by means of the men of the army, so that Jerusalem would lose her fortification and protection and could not resist Babylon.

52.12.0.en: Nebuzaradan chose everyone he saw who was energetic or strong or of distinguished character from among the poor of the people, as well as those who wished to surrender themselves to Babylon, and took them all as captives to Babylon. He left in Jerusalem and its surroundings a group of the poor who worked as farmers to work the land and keep it, but who had no strength to carry out a revolt against Babylon.

52.13.0.en: What remained in the temple of the Lord were the brass works, the most important of which were the two brass pillars, the brazen sea in which the priests used to wash, and likewise the bases of the pillars.

52.14.0.en: Caldrons: large brass vessels in which meat or ashes are placed.

52.14.1.en: Shovels: the plural of shovel, a brass scoop for gathering the ashes from the altar of brass. Snuffers: the plural of snuffer, one of the tools of the altar of brass.

52.14.2.en: Bowls: a small vessel that may be of brass, silver, or gold, with which blood is poured. Spoons: small dishes of brass or gold.

52.14.3.en: Basons: vessels for gathering blood in.

52.14.4.en: Firepans: golden vessels for putting coals and incense in.

52.14.5.en: Candlesticks: the plural of lampstand, which is of gold and is lit with oil.

52.14.7.en: Nebuzaradan took all the vessels of the temple, small or large, made of gold or silver or brass.

52.15.0.en: In these verses he makes clear the huge quantities of brass that Nebuzaradan took from the temple, whether in the pillars and their bases or in the sea and its bases made in the form of bulls. He makes clear the measurements of the brass pillar, whose height was eighteen cubits, about nine meters, whose circumference was about twelve cubits, and whose thickness was 4 fingers, about 7 cm, and the chapiter on the pillar, whose height was five cubits, with network upon the chapiter and pomegranates numbering one hundred. All this was made of pure brass, so the weight of the brass was very great.

52.15.1.en: Sin strips you of all your pride and glory, so hasten to repentance to regain your sonship and your glory as a child of God, and return to the way of life and the striving in the way of the Kingdom.

52.15.2.en: [4] The killing of the priests and the captivity of the people (vv. 24-30)

52.15.3.en: 24- And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:

52.15.4.en: 25- He took also out of the city an eunuch, which had the charge of the men of war; and seven men of them that were near the king's person, which were found in the city; and the principal scribe of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city. 26- So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and went

52.15.5.en: ... to the king of Babylon to Riblah. 27- And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of his own land. 28- This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews and three and twenty: 29- In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred thirty and two persons: 30- In the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred forty and five persons: all the persons were four thousand and six hundred.

52.16.0.en: Nebuzaradan seized the rest of the great men in Jerusalem. He took the priest Seraiah, the foremost, and the priest next to him, Zephaniah, and likewise the keepers of the door of the temple, who were three of the priests, in addition to the eunuch in charge of the men of war, who represents the minister of defense. He also seized seven men of the king's counselors, and the scribe who gathers the men of war for conscription, and added to them sixty men who were the greatest he found among the people.

52.17.0.en: After Nebuzaradan seized the great men who were in Jerusalem, he brought them to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who tortured them and then killed them in Riblah, where he was staying.

52.18.0.en: In this verse and the following verses he mentions those whom Nebuchadnezzar took captive to Babylon, in three stages. The first stage was the captivity of 3023, and this was in the seventh year of Nebuchadnezzar, that is, in the year 598 BC. It is noted that this number is of men only, apart from the women and children, who are all mentioned in (2 Kgs 24:14-16), and this, of course, is apart from those he killed.

52.19.0.en: The second stage of the captivity was of 832 men, and that was in the year 587 BC, in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

52.20.0.en: As for the third stage of the captives, it was of 745 men, and that was in the twenty-third year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, that is, in the year 582 BC, in the days of Gedaliah, whom the king of Babylon appointed governor over Jerusalem. Thus the total number of men taken captive to Babylon was 4600.

52.20.1.en: Do not shatter the strength of others so that you alone remain strong, because God is able to strengthen them and restore their glory to them, as He brought His people back from captivity. And to the extent that you are gentle with others, God supports you and is gentle with you.

52.20.3.en: 31- And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, in the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year of his reign lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and brought him forth out of prison,

52.20.4.en: 32- And spake kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon, 33- And changed his prison garments: and he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life. 34- And for his diet, there was a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon, every day a portion until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

52.21.0.en: Jehoiachin, king of Judah, remained in prison after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took him captive to Babylon, until he had completed 37 years in prison. Then Nebuchadnezzar died and his son Evilmerodach reigned over Babylon. He wished to show his good administration and his kindness toward his subjects, so he brought Jehoiachin out of prison to live with him in his palace, and even gave him more honor than the kings or governors who were imprisoned with him, and brought them out as well, as a proclamation of the mercy of the new rule, especially since Jehoiachin had reached the age of eighty, his people in Jerusalem had become poor and weak, and the Jews in Babylon had settled and acquired property and their inclination to return to Jerusalem had weakened. That is, there was no longer any danger of Jehoiachin carrying out a revolt against Babylon.

52.22.0.en: Jehoiachin lived in the palace of the king of Babylon and ate food at his table, and a salary was given him to spend as he wished, that is, he lived honored until the end of his life in Babylon. This was a prelude to the return of the people from captivity, that is, God is able to free the king and his people from slavery and fetters.

52.22.1.en: Be confident in the power of God, who is able to lift tribulations from you however heavy they may be, and even turns tribulations into blessings, so that you are freed from your sins and receive the reward of your bearing tribulations with thanksgiving.
